fidelity: F2a — RC-Ladder + Voltage-Dependent Faradaic Pseudocapacitance + Redox Kinetics + Thermal ODE
description: Physics-lumped pseudocapacitor (e.g. RuO2 / MnO2 / conducting polymer). Combines an electrostatic double-layer capacitance with a voltage-dependent FARADAIC pseudocapacitance C_far(V) from fast, reversible proton-coupled redox surface reactions. A two-branch RC ladder (fast accessible surface + slow porous/bulk redox sites) reproduces the rate-dependent capacitance loss at high current. Charge-transfer (redox) kinetics via Butler-Volmer limit usable pseudocapacitance at high rate. Leakage from faradaic side reactions, and a lumped thermal ODE (Joule + reversible entropic redox heat) integrated with scipy.solve_ivp.
source: Conway, B. E. (1999). Electrochemical Supercapacitors: Scientific Fundamentals and Technological Applications. Kluwer Academic/Plenum, New York. Chs. 10-11 (pseudocapacitance, C(V)).

cell.name: Generic RuO2 pseudocapacitor cell, 1 V class (aqueous H2SO4)
cell.source: Conway (1999) Electrochemical Supercapacitors; Trasatti & Buzzanca (1971) J. Electroanal. Chem. 29, A1; Zheng, Cygan & Jow (1995) J. Electrochem. Soc. 142, 2699; Sugimoto et al. (2006) Electrochim. Acta 52, 1742; Simon & Gogotsi (2008) Nature Materials 7, 845

C_dl.note: Electrostatic double-layer capacitance (non-faradaic). EDLC contribution is roughly voltage-independent. For RuO2 the EDL is a minor fraction (~15-25%) of total stored charge; the rest is faradaic.

C_far0.note: Baseline faradaic pseudocapacitance scale at the redox mid-potential. Total low-rate capacitance C_dl + ~C_far0 ~ 200 F (matches F1 RuO2 cell). RuO2 cells report 720-900 F/g; here lumped to a 200 F module.

esr_ref.note: Series (ohmic) ESR at T_ref: electrolyte + contact + bulk electronic resistance (~5 mOhm). Source: Zheng et al. (1995).

R_ct_ref.note: Linearised charge-transfer (redox) resistance of the slow porous branch at T_ref. Governs high-rate pseudocapacitance fade. Source: Conway (1999) Ch.11 EIS of RuO2.

v_max.note: Rated voltage for RuO2 in H2SO4 (window ~1 V). MnO2 in neutral electrolyte also ~1 V.

v_redox.note: Centre of the redox pseudocapacitance peak (mid of 0-1 V window). RuO2 shows a broad, nearly rectangular CV from a series of overlapping surface redox transitions centred mid-window. Source: Conway (1999); Trasatti & Buzzanca (1971).

v_width.note: Half-width of the Gaussian-broadened faradaic C(V) hump. Reflects the spread of redox site energies giving the broad mirror-image CV of RuO2.

leakage_resistance.note: Self-discharge resistance; pseudocapacitors leak more than EDLC due to faradaic side reactions / parasitic redox. Source: Simon & Gogotsi (2008).

E_a_esr.note: Activation energy for series ESR (faradaic charge-transfer activation at RuO2 surface, higher than EDLC's ~8 kJ/mol). Source: Sugimoto et al. (2006); Zheng et al. (1995).

E_a_ct.note: Activation energy of the redox charge-transfer resistance R_ct. Redox kinetics are more strongly thermally activated than ohmic transport. Source: Conway (1999) Ch.11.

alpha_C.note: Capacitance temperature coefficient (~0.4%/K). Pseudocapacitance rises with T via improved proton/ion kinetics. Source: Conway (1999); Sugimoto et al. (2006).

dOCV_dT_specific.note: Entropic coefficient for RuO2 + H+ + e- <-> RuO(OH) proton insertion (~-0.2 mV/K). Drives reversible heat. Source: Conway (1999); Trasatti & Buzzanca (1971).

m_cell.note: Lumped cell thermal mass (50 g module incl. electrodes, electrolyte, packaging).

cp_cell.note: Effective specific heat (carbon/RuO2 + aqueous electrolyte + casing average).

hA_cool.note: Natural-convection heat-transfer coefficient times surface area to ambient.

temperature.note: -30 to 60 degC; narrow due to aqueous electrolyte
